experiment: Exp 32 — spectral pruning criterion (P1 applied to a trained GPT-2)

protocol.lmin: per-head lambda_min of the unit-normalized key-gram at the square point
protocol.importance: KL divergence of next-token distribution when the head is ablated (0-ed) at the block output, GPT-2 124M, single text

pre_registered: P1: heads with lmin*T^2 < c are the pruning-redundant ones (pruning literature cross-check pending)
verdict: SUPPORT for the spectral pruning criterion: the 12 least-important heads have mean lambda_min 50x smaller than the 12 most-important; 9/12 of the least-important heads are already rank-collapsed (lmin < 1e-4) vs 0/12 of the most-important. lambda_min is a ZERO-TRAINING head-importance signal at the square point.
honest_label: single text, single model (GPT-2 124M), Spearman 0.558 strong, Pearson 0.18 weak-but-significant (outlier-driven). Cross-check vs pruning literature (Michel 2019: 'are 16 heads really needed?') is the pre-registered next step. Not yet a deployment-ready pruning tool: needs multi-text robustness.
